elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 10.4 instead provides that all programs and writings created by M&I in performing the Services are M&I's sole property.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment to Customer; M&I expressly retains ownership of Developed Software.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 17.2 denies Customer rights in M&I-provided software, systems, documentation, procedures, and related materials except for the stated use and licence rights.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 makes the Developed Software licence perpetual, but does not expressly license pre-existing or other Vendor IP embedded in the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Developed Software licence is irrevocable, but embedded Vendor IP is not expressly included in its scope.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The Developed Software licence is royalty-free, but embedded Vendor IP is not expressly included in its scope.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 17.1 states that Customer remains the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 17.4 expressly limits M&I's use of Customer Data solely to providing the Services.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause creates no joint ownership: Developed Software is M&I's sole property and Customer Data is Customer's sole and exclusive property.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 10.4 makes M&I the sole owner of its programs, ideas, know-how, and concepts, while Section 17.2 preserves M&I's systems and related materials.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 grants Customer a perpetual licence to the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly makes the Developed Software licence irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly makes the Developed Software licence worldwide.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 expressly makes the Developed Software licence royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 permits Customer to use and modify the Developed Software for Customer's business.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Section 10.5 permits Customer to sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 17.4 expressly limits M&I's use of Customer Data solely to providing the Services.
